ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+3$ ($a\neq 0$) intersects the x-axis at points $A(1,0)$ and $B(-3,0)$, and intersects the y-axis at point $C$. Line $BC$ is drawn, intersecting the axis of symmetry of the parabola at point $E$, with the vertex being point $D$. What is the area of $\triangle BOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given equation (1), $y=-x^{2}-2x+3$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point C are $(0,3)$,\\
$\therefore$ OC$=3$,\\
$\because$ the coordinates of point B are $(-3,0)$,\\
$\therefore$ OB$=3$,\\
$\because$ $\angle$BOC$=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of $\triangle BOC$ is $\frac{OB \cdot OC}{2}=\frac{3\times 3}{2}=\boxed{\frac{9}{2}}$.
